title: Bloom Objective Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Bloom's Taxonomy
Objective Classification
Learning Outcomes
Bloom Verbs
description: A p5.js drag-and-drop sorter in which learners classify 24 learning outcomes from the course description into the six Bloom levels using the three-step classification procedure, with verb highlighting, rationales, and defensible neighboring levels for ambiguous outcomes when the learner chooses the matching reason.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers and learning-technology developers

educational.topic: Classifying learning objectives by Bloom level
learningObjectives: Demonstrate the three-step objective classification procedure on real course-description outcomes.
Give a reason for each placement, including ambiguous outcomes.

controls.label: Bins, procedure panel and reason choices

assumptions: Official levels are the headings under which docs/course-description.md lists each outcome.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Modeled procedure, guided practice, then independent practice
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Sorting into category bins with explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: What must the learner actually do with the content?
When two levels are plausible, which is the most demanding process the task truly requires?
commonMisconceptions: The first verb alone decides the Bloom level.
A verb that is missing from the verb table cannot be classified.
Every outcome has exactly one defensible level.
assessmentOpportunities: Counts of correct, defensible and missed placements.
Written three-step classifications for instructor-chosen outcomes.
